A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AFLOW and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite expanded appendices and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–D report original benchmark evaluations, operator ablations, workflow case studies, and cost measurements.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix F adds original novel-generation and academic-idea-generation experiments with LLM and human ratings.

M1.justification: Appendix F adapts AFLOW by revising the optimizer prompt and replacing task-specific scoring with GPT-4o judge feedback for open-ended tasks. The underlying MCTS procedure remains unchanged. Explicitly naming Custom clarifies a component already used in v1.

E1.justification: The six original reasoning, coding, and QA benchmarks are retained. Appendix F adds substantially different task requirements: long-form novel generation using one prompt and academic idea generation using ten questions, both without reference answers.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1 and 2 is unchanged, including ADAS in Table 1. The new open-ended cases reuse direct LLM invocation, an existing baseline. Newly cited research is not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces reference-free evaluation using four 1–5 rubric scores, three human annotators, and task-specific optimizer/executor assignments. Original benchmark splits, metrics, and iteration budgets are retained. Conflicting selection constants in v2 prevent establishing whether that setting changed in the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds open-ended workflow/output case studies and comparisons between human and LLM rankings. Appendix C.2 adds MATH formatting analysis, reporting 55 comma-separated answers in round 13 versus 43 and 42 in better-performing rounds. The original GSM8K ablation and Appendix B case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify split seed 42, five validation executions with mean and standard deviation, and three test executions with averaged results. New rating tables provide means and ranks without adding uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-search information. The annotator count describes the new evaluation sample.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, existing benchmark curves, MATH trajectory scores, and Appendix D costs are unchanged. Tables A1–A2 newly report scores, rankings, and costs across eight rounds: human means rise from 2 to 19.3 for novel generation and from 15.6 to 19.1 at the best idea-generation round. These are new results under added settings.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds assumptions about representational completeness, bounded evaluation, and nonzero expansion probabilities, together with claims of arbitrary-workflow reachability and finite-iteration optimality. These substantially extend the theoretical assertions beyond v1's formulation and selection equation, although no supporting proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: code-represented workflow optimization, MCTS search, superior six-benchmark performance, and improved cost effectiveness. The 5.7% and 19.5% improvement claims remain unchanged. The conclusion's new Appendix F reference does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explanations attributing particular MATH gains and failures to computational tools, review steps, and answer-formatting instructions. Appendix F discusses subjective evaluation through human preferences and interprets the new creative-task results as quality and efficiency gains. These materially expand the earlier interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds open-ended optimizer/judge prompts, generated workflow code, model assignments, annotation details, and an execution-feedback prompt. Selection constants conflict: Section 4 gives alpha=0.4 and lambda=0.2, while Appendix A.6 gives alpha=0.2 and lambda=0.4; v1 specified lambda=0.4 in its appendix. Explicit repository links are replaced by unspecified publication-time release promises.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds positioning relative to workflow benchmarking, multi-agent architectures, and dynamically adjusted workflows, citing Qiao, Zhang, and Niu and colleagues. Appendix F adds role-playing and LLM-as-judge references. The main positioning against ADAS and GPTSwarm is retained.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 clarify code-represented edges, Custom, and the distinction between workflow search nodes and individual LLM nodes. Contributions become an inline list, and Appendix C gains experience and feedback subsections. These are focused revisions within the retained main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A1–A2 and prompt/output boxes, redisplays the existing MBPP workflow in Appendix A.5, relocates Table 2, and relabels indices in Figure 3. Main plot designs and data displays are largely retained, with conference headers and spacing adjustments.

improvement.justification: Added workflow explanations, feedback analysis, and human-rated open-ended cases improve clarity and broaden the evidence. However, v2 introduces contradictory selection constants and an unsupported finite-iteration optimality assertion in Appendix G. The novel also receives the maximum LLM score despite its reported 27,000 words exceeding the exact 20,000-word requirement. These benefits and new reliability concerns leave the net quality change uncertain.
